seoTitle: Change Your Hostinger Domain Name for Free
metaDescription: Update the domain name attached to your Hostinger website through hPanel, with a warning about email data before you start.
intro: Rebranding a project or swapping a placeholder domain for the real one doesn't require a new hosting plan on Hostinger — you can point your existing website at a new domain name from inside hPanel in a few clicks. The one catch is that the switch resets anything tied to the old domain, including your email inboxes and any backups, so it pays to know exactly what the confirmation screen is telling you before you click through it. This guide follows the process screen by screen: finding the setting, reading the warning correctly, and completing the change.

steps.heading: Log in to your Hostinger account
steps.body: Go to Hostinger's website and use the login button in the top right to sign in with your account email and password. If you've forgotten your password, the login form has a reset link right there. Once you're authenticated, Hostinger drops you straight into hPanel, the control panel where every hosting, domain, and email setting for your account lives.

steps.heading: Start from the hPanel home screen
steps.body: hPanel's home page greets you by name and shows a to-do list plus a summary of your active services — hosting plans, VPS instances, and so on. The left sidebar is the main navigation for the rest of this process: Websites, Domains, Emails, and Billing all sit here. You don't need to configure anything on this screen; it's just the jumping-off point for finding the site whose domain you want to change.

image.caption: The hPanel home screen after logging in, with the sidebar — Websites, Domains, Emails — running down the left side.

steps.heading: Open Websites and find the right site
steps.body: Click Websites in the sidebar to see every site attached to your hosting account, each listed with its current domain, plan, and quick-action buttons for tools, WP Admin, and its dashboard. If you manage more than one site, use the search bar at the top to filter by domain or name rather than scrolling through the full list. Confirm you've found the correct entry before continuing, since the domain change you're about to make only applies to the site you select here.

image.caption: The Websites list in hPanel, showing every site on the account with its own row of management options.

steps.heading: Open the three-dot menu and select Change domain
steps.body: Each website row ends with a three-dot icon that opens a menu of extra actions: Add to favorites, Add tag, Change domain, Website Details, and Delete. Click Change domain. If the site is still running on a temporary Hostinger-assigned address, you'll also see a banner right on the row itself reading "Current domain is temporary," with the same Change domain link — either path gets you to the same place.

image.caption: The three-dot menu on a website row, with Change domain listed alongside Website Details and Delete.

steps.heading: Read the warning and confirm you understand it
steps.body: This is the step that trips people up. The Change Website's Domain dialog spells out three consequences before it lets you proceed: your email plan resets and any mailboxes on the current domain are deleted, associated subdomains are removed (though your files are untouched), and existing website backups tied to the current domain are lost and can't be restored. Export any email you need and note down anything backup-related before you tick the checkbox confirming you understand, since there's no undo once you click Change.

image.caption: The Change Website's Domain confirmation dialog, listing exactly what gets reset — email, subdomains, and backups — before you can proceed.

steps.heading: Enter your new domain and finish the switch
steps.body: After confirming, you're prompted to type the new domain name. Enter it carefully — a typo here means repeating the whole process, and your domain is core to your brand and every link you've already shared. Click Next to complete the change. The website is now attached to the new domain, but full worldwide propagation can take anywhere from a few minutes to a couple of days, so don't panic if the new address doesn't resolve everywhere immediately. If something looks wrong after propagation finishes, Hostinger's support team can check the DNS records on their end.

faq.question: Will changing my domain delete my email data?
faq.answer: Yes. Hostinger's confirmation dialog states that your email plan resets and any mailboxes tied to the current domain are deleted, so export anything important before you confirm the change.

faq.question: Are my website files and backups affected?
faq.answer: Your site's files are not touched, but existing backups linked to the current domain are lost and can't be restored once you switch. Any subdomains attached to the old domain are also removed.

faq.question: How long does it take for the new domain to work everywhere?
faq.answer: Propagation varies by network and location, so the new domain may not resolve immediately worldwide. Give it some time before assuming something's broken.

faq.question: Where do I find the Change Domain option?
faq.answer: Go to Websites in hPanel, find your site, and click the three-dot icon at the end of its row. Change domain is listed there, and it also appears as a banner link if the site is still on a temporary domain.

faq.question: What if I run into issues after changing my domain?
faq.answer: Reach out to Hostinger's support team if the new domain isn't behaving as expected once propagation has had time to complete.
